payload.claim: No test drives `cli.main([..., "watch", ...])` down the `UnknownTask` path at all — the only CLI-level watch test (`tests/test_cli.py::test_watch_reads_the_batch_tree_the_cli_already_computes`) stubs `follow` to return `iter(())`, so it never raises. The exact edit `except UnknownTask: print(...); return 1` down to nothing (letting `UnknownTask` propagate) keeps every test green: it would be caught by the outer `except Exception as broke: ... return 2` already in `main` (line ~144-151), silently turning the exit code this spec deliberately chose (1, argued over three lines of comment as distinct from 2) into 2. The acceptance criterion 'exits non-zero' would still technically hold, but the specific, called-out design decision — that a mistyped spec id must not read as infrastructure failure — has zero test coverage at the only layer (the CLI) where that promise is actually kept or broken; `follow`'s own test only checks that `UnknownTask` is raised, not what `cli.main` returns for it.
